item.description: MIAMI, FL - NOVEMBER 13: James Harden #1 of the Cleveland Cavaliers handles the ball during the game against the Miami Heat during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 13, 2026 at Kaseya Center in Miami, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Issac Baldizon/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Miami Heat probably salivated when they saw the injury report and noted the lack of bigs on the Cleveland Cavaliers ’ roster. Evan Mobley was announced out on Thursday with a toe injury . Early on, it looked as if they would be able to survive his absence on Friday night. However, as the game progressed in Miami, the issues only compounded. Despite a decent first half by James Harden (20 points) and Donovan Mitchell (25 points), the Cavaliers’ offense was too dependent on outside shooting. The Cavaliers were relying heavily on one big man on the floor throughout the game. Against most teams, this might be a fine approach. However, the Miami Heat boast a lineup with Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo. The Heat’s All-Star duo gave the Cavaliers fits all night, running downhill and providing a huge problem that they just didn’t have the personnel to stop. The Cavs were constantly having their smaller wings and guards tossed into switches that would see them in mismatches that resulted in good looks for both Giannis and Bam. The Cavaliers, without Mobley’s defensive presence, were not up to the task. Bam (37 points on 13-for-19 shooting) and Giannis 37 points on 15-for-20 shooting) heavily contributed to the Heat’s 54 points in the paint,. The Cavaliers were not able to generate nearly enough offense inside to match Miami’s output, scoring 40 points in the paint by comparison. There were some bright spots for the Cavaliers. Tyrese Proctor (22 points), Meleek Thomas (12 points), and Jaylon Tyson (16 points) all contributed with timely buckets and reliable shooting on a night where the Cavaliers were playing catch-up for the whole second half. A loss like this stings. It felt like they were generating positive momentum and turning the page from the early season struggles after their big win against the New York Knicks. However, losing Mobley and facing an imposing frontcourt like Miami’s halted any forward progress. The Cavaliers look to turn the page when they face the Dallas Mavericks Saturday night in Cleveland.

item.title: Blue Jays’ Anthony Santander apologizes after sharing controversial social media posts
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Blue Jays’ Anthony Santander apologizes after sharing controversial social media posts appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Toronto Blue Jays slugger Anthony Santander has issued a public apology after facing heavy backlash for a pair of anti-Muslim social media posts . In a statement shared on his Instagram story, Santander acknowledged that he should have been more careful with what he posted. “After taking time to reflect on my recent social media posts and speaking with people I trust and respect, I recognize that I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared on my platform,” Santander wrote. “I realize that this content caused hurt and I sincerely apologize.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 32-year-old also addressed the Muslim community directly. “As a man of faith, it is my belief that every person deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their religion, background, or beliefs. After hearing feedback from those I hurt, I realize that the content I shared fell short of my own convictions,” he added. “I would like to affirm my respect for the Muslim community and for the dignity and freedom of people of every faith and background.” Santander’s apology comes after he shared two posts during election week, one of which said “America voted for Sharia last night,” while the other said “Islam is not peaceful.” The posts drew immense criticism from fans and the public. The Blue Jays responded swiftly. On Thursday, the team met with leaders in Toronto’s Muslim communities, and CEO Mark Shapiro released a statement condemning the posts. “We condemn Islamophobia and all forms of hate,” Shapiro said. “The Blue Jays are deeply sorry to the Muslim community and our fans for the pain and harm these Islamophobic posts have caused.” Santander closed his statement by vowing to do better moving forward. “From this experience, I have learned to ensure that none of my communications promote hate or give the impression that I support hatred, discrimination, or violence against anyone,” he wrote. The controversy adds to what has already been a difficult stretch for Santander in Toronto. The former All-Star signed a five-year, $92.5 million contract with the Blue Jays in January 2025, but he missed the entire 2026 season after undergoing left labral surgery in February . item.title: Buddy Hield passes Kyle Lowry on all-time 3-point list
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Buddy Hield passes Kyle Lowry on all-time 3-point list appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bulls needed something to feel good about as they played the Atlanta Hawks on Friday. They were without Caleb Wilson due to a broken hand , which will keep him out for at least six weeks. However, guard Buddy Hield provided some positivity by surpassing Kyle Lowry on the all-time 3-point list. Hield is now No.14 with 2,210 3-pointers. He is now behind Jamal Crawford, Jason Terry, Vince Carter, and Kevin Durant to reach the top 10. Buddy Hield is now No. 14 in NBA history in threes made, passing Kyle Lowry on the all-time list. pic.twitter.com/O4TpjtaawO Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Chicago Bulls (@chicagobulls) November 14, 2026 Before the season started, the Bulls acquired Hield in a 3-way trade with the Charlotte Hornets and Atlanta Hawks, where Hield had played before. He brings sharp shooting, especially from the outside, which Chicago has needed for a while. Hield is averaging 5.8 points per game and is shooting 48.6% from the field. He has played in eight games, and with the roster adjustments being made following Wilson’s absence, Hield has ample opportunity to contribute. He last played on October 30 against the Boston Celtics, in which he played 17 minutes and scored 5 points, and the Bulls lost 125-111. The Bulls are 1-9 and experiencing an eight-game losing streak. The New Orleans Hornets drafted Hield in 2016 out of the University of Oklahoma. He was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team in 2017 and won the 2020 3-point contest during the NBA All-Star Weekend in Chicago. The Bulls are beginning the group stage of the NBA Cup on Friday. As this story is being published, Chicago leads Atlanta 83-79 with under two minutes left in the 3rd quarter. Hield has scored 7 points in seven minutes. item.title: Florida State’s defense shines in road win over Pitt as Seminoles get back to .500
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PA - NOVEMBER 13: Pittsburgh Panthers running back Damon Ferguson Jr. (26) is tackled by Florida State Seminoles defensive lineman Daniel Lyons (5) and Florida State Seminoles linebacker Omar Graham Jr. (9) during the first quarter of the college football game between the Florida State Seminoles and Pittsburgh Panthers on November 13, 2026, at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, PA. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Florida State’s road woes are behind them as the Seminoles (5-5, 3-4) traveled to Pittsburgh Friday night and defeated Pitt (6-4, 3-4), 16-10, for their second straight win away from home. This contest was never going to be pretty, but FSU’s defense, led by interim defensive coordinator Ernie Sims, brought its hard hat and lunch pail to the Steel City and stole a win for the Seminoles. Florida State held the Panthers to only 4.3 yards per play and 5-for-15 on third downs. The Seminoles also had an interception and turned Pitt over on downs three times, giving the offense short fields in a game where field position was paramount. FSU did catch a break with Pitt forced to start true freshman Corey Dailey on short notice, but Sims deserves a ton of credit for switching FSU’s defensive structure to a 4-2-5 in less than two weeks and having his unit ready to play. On offense, Ashton Daniels and company did enough to manage the game and push the Noles over the line. While it wasn’t the prettiest effort, Daniels averaged 10.9 yards per completion, and the offense rushed for 72 yards in the second half after rushing for only 25 in the first. Daniels committed an ill-timed fumble on a controversial call in the fourth quarter, but he otherwise played a clean game and let his defense take over. Florida State is back to .500 for the first time since defeating Central Arkansas in September and finally seems to have an identity on both sides of the ball. As mentioned, FSU didn’t earn any style points for this win, but it would be hard to say the previous administration could have gone on the road, on a short week and won after trailing at the half. Rick Stockstill, Sims and offensive coordinator Tim Harris Jr. deserve a ton of credit for the work they have put in over the two weeks since Mike Norvell’s firing. The game certainly started as expected between a team with an interim head coach on a short week and a freshman quarterback on the other. item.title: Ex-Celtics Star Kyrie Irving Being Viewed as Trade Candidate Around NBA
item.description: Ex-Celtics Star Kyrie Irving Being Viewed as Trade Candidate Around NBA originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former Boston Celtics guard Kyrie Irving has been on multiple teams throughout his career and has made an impact on many of them. Now with the Dallas Mavericks, Irving is finally back after a tough knee injury that kept him out last season. He looks like the same great player we're used to seeing, but it's not crazy to think the Mavericks could eventually move on from him, depending on how the next couple of months go. Dallas has played decent basketball this season, though it might be a bit ahead of schedule. With youngster Cooper Flagg playing as well as he has, the Mavericks might want to give him playoff experience and really go all in. We'll eventually find out if that's the plan, but if it is, there's absolutely no debate that keeping Irving on the roster at that point would make sense. However, while the Mavericks have said they want to keep Irving around for now, the latest report suggests teams across the league are expected to show interest in him, and there's still some belief he'll be dealt. “Yet when you talk to rival teams about players who would truly change the playoff landscape if they were dealt, and who are widely expected to generate serious interest because of that belief, Irving still tops the list. Never mind that the Mavericks, and Irving for that matter, have shown no signs of wanting a split. Quite the opposite, in fact,” Sam Amick wrote . Multiple teams around the NBA could use a player of Irving's caliber, including one team that could have an impact on the Celtics: the Miami Heat. Miami doesn't look like a great team right now despite landing Giannis Antetokounmpo in the offseason, which could lead them to get desperate and try to overpay for Irving. item.title: Jürgen Klopp alludes to future chances for FC Bayern’s Lennart Karl
item.description: Photo by Getty Images Jürgen Klopp’s Germany squad entered the international break needing two wins to advance to the knockout stage of the UEFA Nations League. Klopp collapsed the massive roster from his first international window into one playable unit and Germany dominated all night on the way to a 3-1 victory in Serbia. As the margins narrow, Klopp will continue to shrink the squad to maximize playing time for the best players. In the postgame interview (via @iMiaSanMia ), Klopp explained the decision making behind his squad selection process. “When you make decisions, you look at all 11 players and consider who’s covered how much ground and who you should take off,” said Klopp. “We had actually wanted to take Derry [Scherhant] off and bring Said El Mala on. But Gruda was having a bit of cramp or something like that, so I can’t just send Said back and tell him to sit down again. We were 3-1 up, and there were around 80 minutes on the clock. I know it’s not particularly nice when young players don’t start or don’t get brought on. But some players were decisive today, and tomorrow it will be others.” In the second half, Klopp opted to only utilize one of four Bayern Munich players sitting on the bench. Tom Bischof got the nod to replace his teammate, Aleksandar Pavlović. Lennart Karl, Nathaniel Brown, and Jonas Urbig watched the final whistle from the sidelines. Klopp singled out Lennart Karl as a “wonderful young man. He’s trained really, really well and is fully integrated into the team. He didn’t play today because the player who played in his position is also very good at football. But there will be many chances to come.” Join the conversation! item.title: Burnt Hills' Calhoun sets program assists record, as Spartans win 13th straight Division 2 volleyball title
item.description: Sean Calhoun of Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake serves against CBA in the Section 2 Division 2 volleyball championships at Schenectady High School in Schenectady, NY on Friday, November 13, 2026. Stephen Weaver/For the Times Union (Stephen Weaver) SCHENECTADY - Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake's starters didn't spend all that much time on the court during Friday night's Section 2 Division 2 boys' volleyball championship match against Christian Brothers Academy, but it was enough for the Spartans to stamp their authority on the match and for senior setter Sean Calhoun to make some program history. The top-seeded Spartans easily dispatched winless CBA 3-0 at Schenectady High School, winning by scores of 25-2, 25-21 and 25-17 to help the program earn its 13th consecutive sectional title. Calhoun was among the Burnt Hills (15-2 overall) players who only played during that dominant first set, but, even in his limited time on the court, the senior did enough to earn a spot in the program's record book. Among the 15 assists that Calhoun dished out during that first set was the 2,905th helper of his career, passing 2011 graduate Jordan Armstrong for the most in Burnt Hills history. Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake are the Section 2 Division 2 volleyball champions after defeating CBA at Schenectady High School in Schenectady, NY on Friday, November 13, 2026. Stephen Weaver/For the Times Union (Stephen Weaver) "It's crazy to me, thinking of all the setters who came before me - especially my brother (Aiden Calhoun). I know he's watching this right now," Calhoun said. Burnt Hills coach Paul Sander kept the approaching milestone a secret from Calhoun, who only found out when Sander called a timeout to stop the match after the senior's 2,905th assist. "We wanted it to be a real surprise for him, a real special event," Sander said. "His family knew, and the players knew, but not him. It was hard, but we kept the secret." "The only thing on my mind was states," Calhoun said. "I want states." After Calhoun and fellow senior Arthur Bowcutt led the Spartans to their overwhelming win in the opening set, it was the team's reserves who played out the final two sets to clinch Burnt Hills' spot in the Division 2 state tournament next weekend in Rochester. Tuckahoe needed somebody to carry the load after graduating a pair of generational playmakers from a team that played for a state title. And the next man up happened to be a slightly undersized junior who runs with the abandon of an naturally oversized fullback. Rambalski scored four touchdowns Friday, leading the Tigers to a 40-7 win over Haldane in the Section 1 Class D championship game. “Honestly, it’s the big boys up front,” he said in deflection mode. “They block for me on every play. They open the holes. I just hit them and burst ino the open field.” The initial contact was often completely dismissed and followed by a jolt of adrenaline. “I’m a power back,” Rambalski added. “I just want to get hit. I want it. I want to get hit.” Tuckahoe has won three straight championships and will face the Section 9 champion, Burke Catholic or Chester at 4:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20 at Mahopac High School. “It means everything,” Tigers linebacker Kilian Curylo said. “It’s our final year, our final ride. I’m just grateful for all the guys around me.” Check back later tonight for complete game coverage. Mike Dougherty covers high school football for The Journal News/lohud. Follow along on Instagram @hoopsmbdlohud . This article originally appeared on Rockland/Westchester Journal News: Section 1 football: Somers back on top in A; Tuckahoe three-peats in D

item.title: FSU football beats Pitt, 16-10, as Seminoles defense steps up
item.description: After snapping a nearly three-year-long road losing streak with a victory over Boston College , Florida State football has now notched back-to-back wins on the road after a 16-10 win over Pitt on Friday, Nov. 13, at Acrisure Stadium. It's the first time the Seminoles have won consecutive road games since 2023, beating Wake Forest and Pitt in back-to-back weeks. With the win, FSU is one victory away from its first bowl game since 2023, and is 2-0 under interim head coach Rick Stockstill. With temperatures as low as the mid-30s in Pittsburgh, the Seminoles (5-5, 3-4 ACC) and Panthers (6-4, 3-4 ACC) played a game befitting the chilly temperatures and venue. In the home of the Steelers, FSU's defense rose to the occasion with a stout performance against a Pitt offense led by third-string true freshman quarterback Corey Dailey. He finished the night with 157 yards on 16-for-34 passing, but his interception, a pass that deflected off the back of Deamonte Diggis and into the hands of Rylan Kennedy, proved costly. FSU's lone touchdown, a one-yard rush from Amari Thomas, came off the pick. FSU's Ashton Daniels protected the football and had minimal impact on the ground (nine rushes for 27 yards) against Pitt's elite run defense. Daniels finished the night 16-of-124 for 163 yards, with the Seminoles finding primary success on screen plays. He had a fumble, which came in the red zone, but it didn't lead to any Pitt points. Here are three takeaways from the Seminoles' victory over Pitt. Seminoles offense struggles to warm up on a cold night in Pittsburgh With the exception of wide receiver Jasen Lopez, the Seminoles got little production from the offense in the first half. Lopez recorded 72 total yards on five receptions, including 58 yards in the first half on three receptions, 46 of which came on a big third-down completion. Despite Lopez setting FSU up at the 10-yard line on that 46-yard reception, it only resulted in a field goal. The Seminoles consistently struggled to find the end zone, which led to multiple field goals. Gabe Panikowski, a week after scoring a touchdown, nailed three field goals: 27 yards, 37 yards, and a 47-yarder. FSU's run game struggled in the first half against the Panthers' top-ranked rush defense, holding the team to a total of 99 yards, including 25 yards in the first half. That number was the least since FSU's clash with Clemson in 2024. The Seminoles rushed for 74 yards in the second half, including a one-yard touchdown run from Amari Thomas, the only touchdown of the game for the program. In the fourth, FSU got advantageous field position after a turnover on downs, but a red zone fumble ruined a potential momentum-swinging drive. Daniels rushed for what would have been first-down yardage on third-and-six, but after he was engulfed in a mass of both Seminoles and Panthers, he fumbled.
